company_name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
model: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route; GAAP earnings after regulatory capital retention, preferred stock deducted in the equity bridge, net debt zero)

inputs.base_revenue_definition: FY2026E CORE total revenue = net interest income + noninterest income (GAAP, not FTE), excluding the Q2 2026 significant items (+$448m Visa exchange-programme gain, -$139m AFS repositioning loss, -$85m Visa B-3 derivative; net +$217m) and $7m of integration costs booked in fee income. FY2026 ends 31 Dec 2026 and is unreported. Build: H1 2026 actual 13,040 GAAP (NII 8,068 + noninterest income 4,972) = 12,830 core; Q3 2026 ~6,575 (guided NII +3-3.5% q/q = ~4,240; fee income -5-5.5% q/q on Q2's 2,279 = ~2,160; other noninterest income $150-200m); Q4 2026 ~6,725 (NIM through 3.00% as guided, fees recovering). Total ~26,130. Cross-check against the July 15 2026 guidance reaffirmed in the Q2 10-Q: NII +15-15.5% on FY2025 14,410 = 16,570-16,640; noninterest income ex-items +9% on 8,689 = 9,470; total = ~26,080 (+~13% ex-items, as guided). FY0 = FY2026E so year 1 = FY2027, one year from the valuation date. The CSV Revenue column (FY2025 23,099) IS total revenue for PNC (us-gaap:Revenues), unlike HBAN/NTRS where it is the ASC-606 fee subset.
inputs.share_count_basis: 398.94m common shares outstanding at 20 Jul 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding; balance sheet 557.29m issued less 157.83m treasury = 399.47m at 30 Jun 2026) LESS an ESTIMATED ~2.3m shares repurchased 20 Jul-30 Sep 2026 (management guided Q3 repurchases at the Q2 pace of ~$610m; ~80% of the quarter at ~$215) PLUS ~1.0m dilutive awards (Q2 2026 basic EPS $4.82 vs diluted $4.81 on 403m diluted weighted average) = ~397.7m fully diluted at the valuation date. Held FLAT thereafter: share-based compensation is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count, and buybacks are a distribution of the FCFE capitalised, not a separate driver. The ~13.9m shares issued for FirstBank (5 Jan 2026) are in the base. REFRESH from the Q3 2026 10-Q cover (due early Nov 2026).
inputs.funding_note: Net debt is held at ZERO by construction. PNC is a Fed/OCC-regulated bank holding company: borrowed funds $85,723m and deposits $449,792m at 30 Jun 2026 are operating funding whose cost is already inside net interest income; interest-earning deposits with banks $22,794m (largely at the Fed) are liquidity held against that funding, not surplus cash. The flow capitalised is free cash flow to equity (net income less capital retained to fund risk-weighted-asset growth at the ~10% CET1 operating target) at the cost of equity, so no debt is deducted and no cash added. total_debt and cash are for audit only. Preferred stock (~$5,877m carrying value = total shareholders' equity 64,008 - common shareholders' equity 58,131; capital table shows $5,879m preferred plus related surplus in Tier 1) is deducted at book in equity_bridge; the flows are therefore total net income (before preferred dividends), NOT net income to common, so the preferred cost is charged exactly once.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026E FCFE ~6,050 = core net income ~8,170 (26,100 revenue - ~15,040 core noninterest expense - ~900 provision = ~10,160 pre-tax x (1 - 19.5%)) LESS ~2,100 of capital retained for ~4.5% ORGANIC RWA growth (retention = g / ROTE ~17.5%, ~26% of NPAT; FirstBank's $26.4bn of assets was paid for with ~13.9m shares plus cash and is the reason CET1 fell from 10.6% to 9.9%, so it is not part of the recurring retention). GAAP FY2026E net income ~7,980 (H1 actual 3,827). Cross-check on distributions: FY2026 common dividends ~2,990 (H1 1,387 paid + $2.00 x ~399m x 2) + preferred ~316 + buybacks ~2,640 (H1 1,418 + ~610 x 2) = ~5,950. reported_fcf = FCFE + share-based compensation so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Statutory operating cash flow (FY2025 4,384; FY2023 10,111; Q1 2025 -509) is loan/deposit/trading movement and meaningless as free cash flow for a bank; the CSV FreeCashFlow column is NOT used. reported_fcf here is the FCFE proxy before the SBC charge.
inputs.sbc_source: ESTIMATED: PNC does not tag us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation and the 10-K Note 17 discloses no expense line. FY2025 10-K Note 17: 1.87m PSUs/RSUs granted at ~$191 (~$357m of grant value, ratable over ~3 years), $256m intrinsic value vested in 2025 ($214m 2024, $219m 2023); 5.27m nonvested units at ~$165 at 31 Dec 2025 (~$870m). Annual expense ~$300m = ~1.15% of FY2026E revenue. Taxes withheld on net-share settlement are inside the treasury-stock line and immaterial. SBC is already inside GAAP noninterest expense, so it is added back to the margin driver and charged again via sbc_pct_path -- net zero on the flow, band narrow.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: interest income IS the banking business, and no cash is added to equity value.
inputs.buyback_note: PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,418m in H1 2026 ($796m Q1, ~$622m Q2); Q3 2026 guided at a similar ~$610m pace. FY2025 $1,338m, FY2024 $687m, FY2023 $651m (CET1 rebuild after March 2023), FY2022 $3,731m. Buybacks are a use of the FCFE capitalised, not an extra source of value.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-20 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover count, less estimated Q3 2026 repurchases)
inputs.book_value_anchor: Common shareholders' equity $58,131m at 30 Jun 2026 less goodwill $13,317m and other intangibles, net of related deferred tax liabilities = tangible common equity $44,378m = TBVPS $111.09 on 399m (company-reported, Q2 2026 earnings release). BVPS $145.52. AOCI -$4,120m is inside equity (CET1 excludes it by election). CET1 9.9% at 30 Jun 2026 vs 10.6% at 31 Dec 2025 (FirstBank) and a ~10% operating target. Q2 2026 ROTCE 17.88% (Q1 15.66%, Q2 2025 15.55%); ROE 13.61%. At the current price the market pays ~1.99x TBV and ~1.52x book.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity in USD, the currency of the flows: 10-year US Treasury ~4.5% (late September 2026) + beta 1.1 x US equity risk premium 5.0% = 10.0%. Beta 1.1 sits below the 1.2 used for HBAN (2026-09-29) because PNC is roughly twice HBAN's size, less NIM-geared (fees ~36-38% of revenue vs ~27%), carries a Category III / near-money-centre deposit franchise that held through March 2023, and has a measured five-year beta of ~1.0-1.2. One rate across all three scenarios; credit-cycle, CRE and capital-rule risk is charged in the bear flows and the 20% bear weight, not stacked as a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (~2,400 branches) are immaterial relative to $64bn of equity; lease cost sits inside noninterest expense and therefore inside the modelled pre-tax margin. No lease line and no lease liability deduction.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are trivial ($53m of equity; ~$55-60m/yr of net income, FY2025 $61m). They are deducted at book in equity_bridge; the ~$0.7bn capitalised value of their share of the flows is ~0.2% of equity value and is left inside the flows (noted, not modelled). The 19.5% cash-tax-rate driver is the guided FY2026 effective rate (FY2025 17.5% = 1,489/8,486; H1 2026 19.8%).
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine (house precedent HBAN 2026-09-29, NTRS 2026-10-02, NAB.AX, IAG.AX, GL). SKILL.md routes a bank to residual income on tangible book; FCFE with retention = NPAT x g/ROTE is the clean-surplus equivalent (FCFE = NPAT x (1 - g/ROTE)), and it goes through the validated slider engine, which also produces the workbook. BVPS-compounding is NOT used: book value is ~23% goodwill/intangibles and swings with AOCI (-$4.1bn). Engine mapping: revenue = NII + noninterest income (core, GAAP); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income (revenue - noninterest expense - provision for credit losses) PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue; sbc_pct_path = 1.15%; da_pct = 0 (depreciation, software and core-deposit-intangible amortisation are inside noninterest expense and are genuine costs for a bank, not add-backs); capex_pct_path = capital RETAINED to fund RWA growth at the ~10% CET1 target = NPAT margin x balance-sheet growth / ROTE; cash_tax_rate_path = 19.5%; wacc = cost of equity 10.0%; net_debt = 0; equity_bridge = preferred stock -5,877 and NCI -53. FY2026E core anchor: revenue 26,100, core noninterest expense ~15,040 (guided +8.5% ex-integration/significant items on FY2025 13,834; GAAP ~15,425-15,460 incl. ~$325m FirstBank integration and the $140m Q2 Foundation contribution), provision ~900 (H1 401 + ~250/quarter; NCOs guided ~$225m/quarter), core pre-tax 38.9% of revenue, core efficiency 57.6%. FY2027 base reconciliation: 26,100 x 1.065 = 27,797 revenue x (41.3% - 1.15%) x (1 - 19.5%) = ~8,990 net income, less ~300 preferred dividends (after the Series S redemption) and ~60 NCI = ~8,630 to common / 397.7m = ~$21.70 GAAP EPS (vs FY2026E GAAP ~$19.1 / core ~$19.6); ROTCE ~19% on ~$46bn average TCE. Residual-income cross-check on tangible book: steady-state P/TBV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (17.5 - 2.5)/(10.0 - 2.5) = 2.0x on tangible common + preferred (~$50.3bn) = ~$100.6bn, less preferred $5.9bn = ~$238/share. The engine base ($254, 2.29x common TBV, 11.7x FY2027E EPS, 1.75x book) sits ~$16 above it because the steady-state formula ignores the FY27-FY31 phase in which revenue compounds at 3.5-6.5% (NIM expansion needs no capital) at a ROTE ~8pp above the cost of equity; the engine's ROTE on year-10 equity is ~17.2%, so no return drift is being capitalised. The market's ~1.99x TBV implies ROTCE ~17.4% in steady state at a 10% cost of equity (the Q2 2026 run-rate with no further NIM expansion), or a ~10.7% cost of equity on the guided trajectory. Price is the NYSE regular close on 1 Oct 2026, not an after-hours print. Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) is unreported (release due mid-Oct 2026); 30 Jun 2026 is the latest balance sheet. Series S preferred ($525m) is called for redemption on 2 Nov 2026 (8-K 2026-09-29): value-neutral (preferred falls $525m, common capital falls $525m), so the bridge keeps the 30 Jun carrying value.

equity_bridge.item: Preferred stock (Series B, S, T, U, V, W, X; carrying value)
equity_bridge.note: Total shareholders' equity 64,008 less common shareholders' equity 58,131 at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q / earnings release); Tier 1 capital table 'preferred stock plus related surplus' 5,879. PreferredStockValue is tagged 0 because PNC carries preferred in capital surplus. Dividends ~$316m/yr (H1 2026 $158m). Deducted at book because the flows are total net income before preferred dividends; at a ~5.4% average coupon versus a 10% cost of equity, book over-states the economic claim by ~$1.5bn (~$4/share) -- conservative, consistent with HBAN/NTRS.

historical_growth.fcf_series_note: For a bank the distributable-earnings series is GAAP net income (already after share-based compensation): FY2020 7,558 (incl. ~$4.3bn after-tax gain on the BlackRock stake sale in discontinued operations, offset by a COVID CECL build); FY2021 5,725 (BBVA USA merger costs); FY2022 6,113; FY2023 5,647; FY2024 5,953; FY2025 6,997 (SEC XBRL ProfitLoss). 3-year CAGR 4.6%, 5-year -1.5% (distorted by the FY2020 BlackRock gain). Revenue (us-gaap:Revenues = NII + noninterest income): FY2020 16,901; FY2022 21,120; FY2025 23,099 -- the 5-year 6.5% is inflated by BBVA USA (closed June 2021); the 3-year 3.0% spans the 2023-24 deposit-repricing trough. Diluted EPS FY2020 16.99 (BlackRock gain), FY2022 13.85, FY2025 16.59. Equity (total equity incl. NCI): FY2020 54,041; FY2022 45,812 (AOCI trough); FY2025 60,636.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case 10-year average revenue growth (6.5% FY27 tapering to 2.5%), bracketed by the 3-year revenue CAGR (3.0%, a deposit-repricing trough window) and the 5-year (6.5%, BBVA-inflated). Equity CAGRs are AOCI swings and acquisition issuance, not compounding.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-year CAGR (9.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (3.0%) and the 5-year (2.3%) from revenue (6.5%): FY2022 book value was depressed by ~$10bn of unrealised AFS losses in AOCI that have since partly unwound, so the 3-year equity CAGR measures AOCI recovery, and the 5-year starts from the post-BlackRock-sale FY2020 peak before the BBVA cash purchase. EPS 5-year is negative only because FY2020 includes the BlackRock gain. Growth is taken from the revenue series and FY2026-27 guidance.

base.growth_rationale: Total core revenue. FY27 6.5%: NII ~+7.5% (average loans +4-5% as second-half 2026 growth 'moderates toward GDP-aligned rates', plus NIM from ~2.97% FY26 average to ~3.05-3.10% as the fixed-rate asset repricing tailwind management cites continues and the Q4 2026 exit is >3.00%) and fees +5% (capital markets normalising from a pulled-forward 2026, card/treasury management/asset management +5-6%). No further acquisition effect: FirstBank closed 5 Jan 2026 and is in FY0 for the full year. FY28 5.0% as the repricing tailwind fades; tapers to 2.5% terminal (nominal GDP less structural deposit-beta creep), bracketing the 3.0% and 6.5% 3/5-year revenue CAGRs.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax income + SBC on revenue. FY26E core: 100 - efficiency 57.6% - provision 3.45% = 38.9% (+1.15 SBC = 40.1). FY27 41.3 = 100 - efficiency 55.7% (core expense +~3%: the $350m continuous-improvement programme and FirstBank synergies against wage/technology inflation; integration costs gone) - provision 4.1% (~30bp on ~$385bn average loans: NCOs now 25bp, plus reserve build for growth and office CRE) + 1.15. FY28 41.5 = efficiency 55.3% - provision 4.3% + 1.15. FY29+ 41.5 = efficiency 55.0% - provision 4.6% (~33bp mid-cycle; loans run ~14x revenue) + 1.15, held. FY2025 actual was 36.7% pre-tax (8,486/23,099) + ~1.2% SBC on a 59.9% GAAP efficiency ratio and 3.4% provision; the path assumes NIM and cost-out deliver ~2.5pp of efficiency gain while credit normalises upward by ~1pp of revenue.
base.capex_rationale: Capital retained to hold CET1 at ~10% as RWA grows = NPAT margin (~32.4% of revenue) x balance-sheet growth / ROTE ~17.8% (total NI incl. preferred over TCE + preferred ~$50bn) = ~1.83 x g, where g is balance-sheet (RWA) growth, which runs ~1.5-2pp below FY27-28 revenue growth because NIM expansion consumes no capital. FY27-28 at 4.5% RWA growth: 8.2% of revenue (~$2.3bn, ~25% of NPAT retained -> ~75% distributed = $8.00 dividend ~$3.2bn + ~$3.2bn of buybacks/preferred, slightly above the current ~$2.4bn/yr buyback pace once CET1 is back at 10%). Steps down with growth to 4.6% at the 2.5% terminal rate (~14% retained). CET1 cross-check: 4.5% growth on ~$488bn of RWA at 10% needs ~$2.2bn.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM reaches ~3.20% by FY28 as fixed-rate assets reprice and the 10-Q's 'risks skewed toward tighter monetary policy' play out for an asset-sensitive balance sheet; Denver/Phoenix (FirstBank) and the BBVA Sunbelt markets take deposit share; commercial loans grow 6-7%; capital markets compound toward management's 25-30% target. Revenue +8% FY27 fading to 3% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 54.6% - provision 4.0% + 1.15 = 42.5. Positive operating leverage of ~2-3pp a year takes efficiency to 52.5% by FY30 (the BBVA-integration-era best was ~58%; peers USB/FITB run ~55-57%, money-centres mid-50s) with credit benign at ~4.0% of revenue (~28bp): 100 - 52.5 - 4.0 + 1.15 = 44.6, held. FY27 EPS ~$23, ROTCE ~20-21%.
bull.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~35% x RWA growth / ROTE ~20% = ~1.75 x g: higher growth needs more capital even at a better return. FY27 at 6% RWA growth retains 10.5% of revenue (~30% of NPAT); FY28 5.5% -> 9.6%; terminal 3% growth retains 5.3% (~15%).

bear.growth_rationale: The Fed cuts faster than the curve implies into a slowdown: asset yields reset while deposit competition (megabanks, high-yield online banks) keeps funding costs sticky, so NIM stalls at ~2.95% instead of breaking 3%; loan growth slows to 1-2% as borrowers de-lever; capital markets fees give back the 2026 pull-forward. Revenue +2% FY27, flat FY28, then 2-3% nominal.
bear.margin_rationale: FY27: efficiency 58.0% (revenue shortfall against a largely fixed cost base; the $350m cost programme offset by technology/compliance) - provision 6.5% (~45bp: office CRE -- 29.4% criticized and 8.1% nonperforming on a $5.1bn book -- migrating into the broader $36bn CRE book, plus seasoning of the acquired FirstBank loans) + 1.15 = 36.6. FY28 credit cycle: provision 10.0% (~70bp; FY2020 COVID was 3,175 = 18.8% of revenue, so this is a mid-sized cycle, not a crisis) with efficiency 59.0%: 32.1. FY29 provision 7.0%, efficiency 58.5%: 35.6. Recovers to provision 6.0% (~42bp) and efficiency 58.0%: 37.1, held -- no operating leverage. FY27 EPS ~$18.5, FY28 ~$16; ROTCE ~13-15%.
bear.capex_rationale: Retention = NPAT margin ~29% x RWA growth / ROTE ~14% = ~2.1 x g. FY27-29 held at 5.5-6.0% despite 0-2.5% growth because RWA migration in a downturn, a Basel III endgame re-proposal and rebuilding CET1 from 9.9% to the 10% target consume capital the model must top up (the 2023 precedent was a buyback cut to ~$650m/yr, not a raise). FY30 6.3% at 3% growth; terminal 2% growth retains 4.2%.

scenario_narratives.base: PNC banks the FirstBank conversion (completed June 2026), pushes NIM through 3% as fixed-rate assets reprice, and grows revenue ~6.5% in FY2027 fading to 2.5% as loan growth settles at GDP-like rates. The $350m cost programme and integration synergies bring the core efficiency ratio from ~57.6% to ~55%, while provisions normalise from today's ~25bp NCO rate to ~33bp mid-cycle. GAAP EPS reaches ~$21.70 in FY2027 (vs ~$19 in FY2026) on a ~19% ROTCE, and ~75-85% of earnings are distributed. At a 10% cost of equity that franchise is worth ~2.3x tangible book (~11.7x FY2027E EPS), against the ~2.0x the market pays.
scenario_narratives.bull: NIM reaches ~3.20% as an asset-sensitive balance sheet meets a Fed leaning tighter, the Sunbelt/Mountain West franchises take deposit share, capital markets compound toward the 25-30% target and positive operating leverage takes efficiency to ~52.5%. Credit stays benign (~28bp). ROTCE reaches 20-21%, EPS compounds high-single-digit, and PNC earns a money-centre-like multiple of tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bear: A faster cutting cycle into a slowdown stalls NIM below 3% while deposit competition keeps funding costs sticky; loan growth stalls and the 2026 capital-markets pull-forward reverses. Office CRE stress (29% criticized) spreads into the wider $36bn CRE book and a mid-sized credit cycle takes provisions to ~70bp in FY2028. Efficiency stays near 58%, ROTCE settles at 13-15% (a modest spread over the cost of equity), and with CET1 below the 10% target buybacks are cut while capital is rebuilt and a Basel III endgame re-proposal lifts requirements.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20%: CET1 is 9.9%, below the ~10% operating target after FirstBank, leaving little buffer for a credit cycle or a Basel III endgame re-proposal; office CRE is visibly stressed (29.4% criticized, 8.1% nonperforming); and the Q2 10-Q itself flags rate risk skewed in both directions. Not raised to the 25% used for HBAN/NTRS because PNC raised rather than cut guidance, its integration is complete, and it is less NIM-geared. Bull cut to 30%: the base already credits NIM >3%, the $350m cost programme and continued capital-markets strength.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A super-regional bank is valued on what it can distribute after funding its regulatory capital, discounted at a USD cost of equity -- never on statutory operating cash flow (loan and deposit movement) and never with deposits or borrowed funds treated as net debt. Core GAAP net income is the flow; capital retention at NPAT x g/ROTE is the reinvestment; preferred stock and NCI are deducted at book so the common claim is valued; 10.0% is the return an owner requires from a diversified, Category-III US bank. The result is the residual-income answer in FCFE form: at a ~18-19% return on tangible common equity, 3.5-6.5% growth fading to 2.5%, PNC is worth ~2.3x tangible book ($111.09) in the base case, so the ~2.0x the market pays embeds roughly the Q2 2026 ROTCE run-rate with little credit for the guided NIM expansion -- modest upside to the weighted value, a bear case ~16% below the price, and the 15%-hurdle entry price well below today's quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net interest margin: 5bp on ~$560bn of average earning assets is ~$280m of NII (~1.1% of revenue, ~2.7% of NPAT); the base needs NIM to break 3.00% in Q4 2026 and keep rising in 2027

Credit cycle: every 10bp on the provision rate over ~$370bn of loans is ~$370m pre-tax (~3.6% of NPAT); office CRE ($5.1bn, 29.4% criticized, 8.8% reserve) and the broader $36bn CRE book are the visible stress, the acquired FirstBank book the unseasoned one
Efficiency: the base assumes ~2.5pp of efficiency improvement from FY26E core 57.6% to 55.0%; every 1pp is ~$280m pre-tax (~2.7% of NPAT)
Capital: CET1 9.9% vs a 10% target; a Basel III endgame re-proposal or a credit-driven RWA migration would force retention above g/ROTE and cut the ~$2.4bn/yr buyback
Share count: the ~2.3m Q3 2026 repurchase estimate is an approximation until the Q3 10-Q cover prints; each 4m shares is ~1% of value per share
SBC is estimated (~$300m) from Note 17 grant values because PNC does not disclose the expense; because it is added back and charged again in the engine, an error here moves value by only cents
Preferred stock is deducted at $5,877m carrying value; the economic value of the ~$316m/yr dividend stream at a 10% cost of equity is lower, so the bridge is ~$4/share conservative

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 176.88-258.96.
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 0000713676) for FY2020-FY2025 and Q1/Q2 2026 NII, noninterest income, noninterest expense, revenue, pre-tax income, income taxes, net income, preferred dividends, NCI, diluted EPS, equity, goodwill, treasury shares, repurchases and dividends; Q2 2026 10-Q (accession 0001628280-26-053170, filed 2026-08-05) for the 30 Jun 2026 balance sheet, provision, significant items, capital ratios/RWA and the reaffirmed Q3/FY2026 guidance; Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, accession 0001628280-26-048244) for TBVPS $111.09, TCE $44,378m, ROTCE and the Foundation/integration expense detail; FY2025 10-K (accession 0000713676-26-000020) for preferred series, Note 17 stock compensation and tax detail; 8-K 2026-09-29 for the Series S redemption; PNC_Metrics.csv / PNC.duckdb (94 periods) for the reported history and kpis (buybacks, cash taxes).
data_sources.qualitative: PNC_Analysis.json (2026-10-02): FirstBank acquisition and June 2026 conversion, Q2 2026 results, NIM >3% year-end guidance, FY2026 guidance (revenue ~+13% ex-items, NII +15-15.5%, fees +9%, expense +8.5% ex-items, ETR ~19.5%), $2.00 dividend, ~$610m/quarter buybacks, office CRE stress, CET1 9.9%, competitive position and bull/bear cases.
